input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 24 meets the preferred position in full: 24.1 lets us assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor consent (notice only); 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our consent (reasonableness-qualified) and never to a direct competitor; and 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on our change of control. Section 24.3's mutual consent requirement is scoped to "other assignments," so it is a residual catch-all and does not swallow the 24.1 carve-out; the consent standard there is also fully qualified ("withheld, conditioned, or delayed"). Section 13.3 reinforces the position by allowing licence rights to travel with a Section 24-permitted assignment. Section 9.2's insolvency termination right is mutual and expressly excludes a lawful reorganization that does not impair performance, so it creates no back-door change-of-control exit. No redline needed.
